summary: Intermittent control-plane mTLS failures caused by transparent proxy rewriting client cert metadata
description:
Issue summary: Customers report intermittent authentication failures from control-plane to serving nodes on a Private deployment. Symptoms are control-plane mTLS handshakes failing with 'client certificate fingerprint mismatch' while artifact downloads and general HTTPS egress appear normal.

Impact: Service control-plane intermittently rejects node heartbeats and agent registration, causing a subset of serving nodes to show 'disconnected' in Console and triggering autoscale churn. Customer reports degraded throughput for background model pulls and delayed rollouts. Approx 3-5% of control-plane handshakes over the last 24h failed.

Environment: Private deployment behind corporate transparent TLS-inspection proxy. Customer enabled proxy-wide TLS interception for outbound traffic to monitor DLP. Control plane endpoints are accessed via vpce/private endpoint (us-east-1).

Steps to reproduce: 1) Deploy a serving node in the customer's VPC with Private package. 2) Ensure corporate transparent proxy intercepts egress and re-issues TLS using inspection cert. 3) Observe control-plane auth logs and serving-node logs. 4) Reproduce by forcing agent restart or network flap.

Observed logs/snippets: - control-plane error: 'tls: peer certificate fingerprint mismatch; expected 2c:9a:... but got 2c:9b:...' - serving node: 'mTLS handshake succeeded, session resumed=false, client_cert_nonce=0x7f2c...' - tcpdump (client->control-plane): ClientHello SNI=control.redwood.local; proxy rewrites TLS and injects X-Client-Nonce header into sanitized tls-terminated HTTP CONNECT.

First response/triage summary: Support verified customer is using an intercepting proxy (CorpProxy v4.8) that terminates TLS and re-issues server cert. During inspection the proxy rewrites a TLS extension (we observed a custom 'client nonce' extension) and replaces the client certificate metadata presented to the control-plane mTLS verification component. Unlike truncation bugs we've seen before, the proxy substitutes a freshly-generated inner certificate representation in the proxied session which preserves subject fields but alters the certificate public-key fingerprint and session ticket. This triggers a fingerprint mismatch on control-plane side when the serving node attempts to authenticate using resumed sessions or certificate-pinned identity.

Hypothesis: The proxy performs active TLS termination and re-originates a new TLS session to the control-plane. For certain handshake paths (session-resumption, 0-RTT, or when client auth is proxied via headers), the proxy injects/rewrites an internal client-certificate metadata blob rather than forwarding the original client cert or performing TLS passthrough. Control-plane expects the original client cert fingerprint or preserved leaf public key for agent identity; the substitution yields intermittent rejects because some agent connections bypass the proxy or use different egress NAT mappings and produce the original cert chain.

Immediate impact mitigation: Requested customer to create an allowlist for control-plane VPCE endpoints to bypass TLS inspection (proxy passthrough) as a short-term workaround. Also suggested turning off session-resumption caching on agents to force full handshake until root cause is resolved.

Files/traces attached: tcpdump trace summary (redacted), control-plane handshake logs, agent debug output (redacted).
investigation_notes:
Timeline of activity: 2026-02-20 09:12 - Customer first reported spike in agent Disconnected alerts. 2026-02-20 10:03 - Support obtained debug bundle from customer (agent logs + tcpdump). 2026-02-20 11:00 - Observed proxy TLS termination in tcpdump; proxy injects HTTP CONNECT with header X-Client-Cert-Metadata. 2026-02-20 12:45 - Reproduced in lab by standing up a test VM behind same proxy (CorpProxy v4.8). 2026-02-20 14:00 - Confirmed fingerprint mismatch patterns correlate with proxied sessions that were re-originated by the proxy (no packet-level corruption). 2026-02-21 09:15 - Eng (SRE) ran a debug build of control-plane auth module with extended logging; logs show control-plane receives client-cert metadata that lacks SubjectPublicKeyInfo equality even when subject DN matches.

Technical findings: - Proxy rewrites certificate metadata instead of forwarding raw client cert during TLS termination+client-auth inspection. - Session resumption paths (TLS tickets) sometimes confuse proxy because it re-issues tickets; resumed sessions occasionally present mismatched public-key fingerprints. - Artifact download traffic (S3 presigned) unaffected because those flows use standard server-auth TLS and are proxied transparently.

Checks performed: - OpenSSL s_client to control-plane endpoint from agent host: full handshake succeeds when proxy bypassed. - OpenSSL s_client when proxy active: intermediate cert chain shows inspection CA as issuer for the server side; client-cert info present only as HTTP header X-Client-Cert-Metadata (proxy-specific). - control-plane logs show auth token validated but certificate-pinning comparison failed on public-key hash.

Next steps planned: - Guidance doc for customers about transparent TLS inspection and Private deployments (draft PR). - Recommend configuration options for common proxies (CorpProxy, BlueTap, Squid with TLS-in-TLS) to preserve client-cert passthrough or apply TCP passthrough for Redwood control-plane endpoints. - Short-term: customer to whitelist control-plane endpoints from interception; Redwood to add diagnostic checks in installer to detect active TLS inspection appliances on bootstrap. - Long-term: evaluate protocol fallback to mTLS over mutually trusted proxy (RFC-compliant header exchange) or provide an agent-side option to use out-of-band client-cert signing for proxied environments.

resolution: Workaround implemented: Customer added VPCE CIDR ranges to proxy bypass list and disabled TLS inspection for Redwood control-plane endpoints. This eliminated ~98% of reported disconnects. Permanent resolution: Documented recommended proxy configs and created installer check to detect active TLS inspection appliances during Private deployment bootstrap. Eng task (INT-9021) opened to explore agent-side mitigation (disable session-resumption by default behind proxied environments and/or sign ephemeral client certs out-of-band). Ticket remains open until customer completes full validation and the installer check PR is merged.
follow_up_actions: Create KB article for configuring common TLS inspection appliances to preserve client-cert passthrough or enable TCP passthrough for control-plane endpoints.
Add installer-time check that detects presence of TLS-inspection/proxy appliances and surfaces a warning during Private deploy.
Engineering task INT-9021: Evaluate agent option to disable TLS session-resumption when transparent proxies detected.
Customer to validate for 72 hours and confirm before we mark Closed.
